2025
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Original Jurisdiction
 Transfer Petition (C) No. 1751/2024
 Abha Sinha ...Petitioner(S)
 Versus
 Prashant Kumar Srivastava ...Respondent(S)
 O R D E R

This Transfer Petition has been filed by the petitioner who is the wife of the respondent, seeking the following prayers:
(a) transfer the Original Suit No.389/2023 titled as Prashant Kumar Srivastava versus Abha Sinha pending before Ld. Principal Judge, Family Courts at Bokaro,
Jharkhand, to the Court of Ld. Principal Judge, Family Courts at Patiala House, New Delhi;
(b) Pass such further order(s) as this Honble Court may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.

sentences.text: 2. During the pendency of this Transfer Petition, the parties were referred to the Supreme Court Mediation Centre.

3. Learned counsel for the respective parties submitted that the parties have decided to part-ways and seek dissolution of their marriage by a decree of divorce on certain terms and conditions which are delineated in the Settlement Agreement dated 09.09.2025.

4. Learned counsel for the respective parties also submitted that a joint application under Article 142 of the Constitution of India has been filed seeking dissolution of the marriage between the parties in view of the settlement arrived at between the parties in terms of the Settlement Agreement dated 09.09.2025 which is supported by the affidavits filed by the respective parties.
5. Respondents counsel submitted that a sum of Rs.24,50,000/-(Rupees Twenty Four Lakhs and Fifty Thousand Only) is being paid by the respondent to the petitioner by way of a demand draft.
The said demand draft is handed over to the learned counsel for the petitioner who has in turn handed over the same to the petitioner who has acknowledged the receipt of the same.

Learned counsel for the respective parties also submitted that two items of jewellery, namely, a gold necklace Abha Sinha vs Prashant Kumar Srivastava on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74762693/
1 (38.740 grams) and a pair of gold earrings (4.000 grams) are handed over by the respondent to the petitioner herein.

sentences.text: The receipt of the same is acknowledged by the petitioner.

6. Therefore, learned counsel for the respective parties submitted that the Settlement Agreement dated 09.09.2025 as well as the joint application filed under Article 142 of the Constitution of India may be taken on record and appropriate orders may be made thereon.
7. The parties are present before this Court.
They have been identified by their respective counsel.

When we queried the parties, they stated that they have indeed arrived at a settlement of all their disputes on certain terms and conditions as delineated in the Settlement Agreement dated 09.09.2025.
They have decided to part ways by seeking dissolution of their marriage by a decree of divorce by mutual consent.
The cases which have been filed by them inter se may also be quashed.
8. They further stated that they have arrived at this settlement on their own free volition without there being any coercion or undue influence on any side.
They also stated that they would abide by the terms of Settlement.
9. In the above backdrop, we have taken on record the Settlement Agreement dated 09.09.2025 as well as the joint application filed under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.
We have perused the same.

10. We have already noted the payment of a sum of Rs.24,50,000/-(Rupees Twenty-Four Lakhs and Fifty Thousand Only) by way of a demand draft by the respondent to the petitioner who has acknowledged receipt of the same.
11. The petitioner has also acknowledged the receipt of two items of gold jewellery.

12. The cases filed by the respective parties are as under:
a) Both the parties hereto confirm and declare that they have voluntarily and mutually of their own free-will, have decided to dissolve their marriage solemnized on 23.01.2022 as per the terms agreed therein between them.
b) That it has been agreed between both the parties that respondent shall pay a total sum of Rs.24,50,000/-(Rupees Twenty Four Lakhs and Fifty Thousand Only) as a full and final settlement to the Petitioner towards her claims/rights qua Stridhan,
maintenance past, present, future, other articles exchanged during their marriage,
residence and permanent alimony.
c) That both the parties herein agree that they shall jointly pray to the Honble Supreme Court in the present Petition to exercise its power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India granting a Decree of Divorce by mutual consent dissolving their marriage solemnized on 23.01.2022 and allowing parties herein to withdraw all the pending litigations amongst them and quash all the pending criminal cases.

sentences.text: d) The respondent shall pay the above stated total sum of Rs.24,50,000/-(Rupees Twenty Four Lakhs and Fifty Thousand Only) as a full and final settlement to the petitioner towards her claims/rights qua stridhan, maintenance past, present and future other articles exchanged during their marriage, residence and permanent alimony by way of DD, to the petitioner at the time of grant of divorce decree by way of mutual consent and quashing/disposal of all the pending litigations amongst the parties herein, by the Honble Supreme Court of India, in case the Honble Court exercises its discretion under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.

9. That the present Settlement Agreement pertains to all pending litigations except Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, as registered vide FIR No.0237/2023 registered with Kishan Garh Police Station Delhi as the offence being non-  compoundable and therefore the parties  state that they shall approach  appropriate forum/Honble Court for the  same.

13. Having perused the Settlement Agreement dated 09.09.2025 as well as the joint application, we find that the terms of settlement are just and proper and there is no legal impediment in accepting the same.
Therefore, we accept the terms of the Settlement.
14. We have perused the joint application filed by the parties under Article 142 of the Constitution of India seeking dissolution of their marriage.
Having perused the said application, we find that the prayers sought for by the parties ought to be accepted and are accepted.
Consequently, the marriage solemnized between the parties on 23.01.2022 at Bokaro, Jharkhand is dissolved by a decree of divorce by mutual consent.
15. Consequently, the aforesaid cases filed by the parties against each other stand quashed.
16. The Settlement Agreement dated 09.09.2025 shall be read as part and parcel of this order.
17. The application filed under Article 142 of the Constitution of India is allowed.
18. The Registry to draw-up a decree in the aforesaid terms.

19. Consequently, the Transfer Petition is disposed of in the aforesaid terms.
20. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

,J.
(B.V. NAGARATHNA) ,J.
